tier_rationale: Manufacturer specifications list Hi-Speed USB 2.0 as the only interface, with no wireless or Ethernet, while sibling models in the same line (HL-L2405W, HL-L2460DW) are sold specifically as the wireless variants.
the_unplug_test: Nothing changes. It is a USB cable and a laser engine. There is no Wi-Fi, no Ethernet, no app, no account, and no subscription prompt during setup. The printer cannot fetch a firmware update on its own because it has no way to reach the internet — any update has to be pushed deliberately from the computer it is plugged into.

repairability.notes: Separate toner cartridge (TN830/TN830XL) and drum unit (DR830), so the drum is not thrown away with every refill. Third-party toner is widely sold — but see the vendor note on Brother's 2025 firmware dispute.

sources.supports: Manufacturer product page lists Hi-Speed USB 2.0 as the only connection method, explicitly no WiFi/wireless/Ethernet. Listed at $134.99, out of stock direct at time of check. No subscription or cloud service mentioned.

Sibling-model control: the HL-L2405W in the same product line is sold with dual-band wireless and Refresh subscription eligibility, confirming that the HL-L2400D's lack of wireless is a deliberate product tier rather than an omission in the spec sheet.

open_questions: Confirm whether Brother's Windows/macOS driver bundle applies firmware updates silently or prompts, since on a USB-only printer the host computer is the only update path.
Verify current third-party toner behaviour on this specific model in light of the 2025 firmware dispute — see the Brother entry in the vendor ledger.
notes: The current-production answer to 'I just want a printer.' Its value is precisely what it lacks: with no network interface, the entire category of printer cloud abuse — mandatory accounts, subscription-gated ink, remote firmware pushes — is structurally unavailable to the vendor.
